name: Paleon
audience: Curious English-speaking viewers interested in ancient daily life, survival and human evolution.
viewer_promise: Explain an answerable question about ancient humans using archaeological and scientific evidence.
topic_scope: Prehistory, ancient daily life, survival and human evolution; specify population, location and period.

editorial.tone: Clear, curious, conversational; avoid unsupported certainty.
evidence_rules: Modern hunter-gatherers are not direct recordings of Paleolithic life.
Evolution is branching, not a ladder toward modern humans.

visual.style_anchor: Hand-drawn 2D doodle cartoon animation, flat solid colors, bold black hand-drawn outlines, slightly wobbly imperfect marker lines,
visual.style_lock: no gradients, no drop shadows, no photographic textures, no photorealism, no 3D render, no anime, 16:9 widescreen, simple educational doodle style.
visual.character: Spiky orange hair #F58220, large round white head with black dot eyes and expressive mouth, no nose or ears, flat white tube torso, thin black stick limbs, white mitten hands; supporting humans share this anatomy, differentiated by hair, flat tunics and props. No realistic skin tones or anatomical volume; use simplified labeled anatomy diagrams when needed.
visual.continuity: Keep characters and props stable across connected scenes. Use flat color blocks for night and firelight rather than gradients.

packaging.style: Dramatic contrast, dark navy background and short text where supported by the episode. Calm evidence close-ups and comparisons remain valid; no CTR superiority is established.
